Senses.Explanation: 呈漆器 means present the lacquerware. Asked what it is like when people of the Way meet, Zhaozhou answers, 'Present the lacquerware.' Xueguan Zhiyin later treats speaking as sharing Zhaozhou's presentation of lacquerware, contrasted with Vimalakirti's silence. Lingshu Yuan raises the exchange and praises its object as all-sided, self-turning, and open in every direction. These receptions make the phrase a recognizable Zhaozhou formula, but do not justify translating away its lacquerware image. Yuan'an Liao applies the same words directly when a monk presents his sitting cloth, confirming that the formula can be turned onto an observable presentation.
Senses.Note: The later praise interprets the response without supplying a stable lexical substitute for 漆器. Do not turn the phrase into 'demonstrate enlightenment' or another doctrinal gloss.
